title: Structured-stream framing: robust escaping, truncation recovery, and retry semantics for JSON tool payloads
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Edge-case handling for streaming structured JSON used for function/tool calling. We see incorrect tool invocations or parse failures when the model emits partial JSON fragments, escapes quotes inside values, or truncates mid-token. This ticket defines robust framing, escape handling, truncation recovery heuristics, and retry/idempotency semantics to prevent duplicate or invalid tool calls across hosted and dedicated runtimes.
motivation: Customer integrations (chatbots and agent frameworks) rely on near-real-time tool calls via streaming. Failures or duplicated calls from malformed partial JSON are high-severity for downstream systems (billing, side-effects). We must make the API resilient across streaming transports (HTTP chunking, SSE, WebSocket) and preserve compatibility with older client SDKs that expect line-delimited JSON or final-block-only semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming parser handles partial JSON chunks across multiple events and reconstructs complete objects without losing escaped characters (" and unicode escapes)
Tool/function call is only emitted once per logical JSON object; retries use an idempotency token derived from stable fields when available
On truncation (connection drop / final chunk loss), clients can resume safely with a byte/sequence token and server will not double-submit side-effecting calls
Backward-compatible mode: if client sets legacy_stream_delta=true, behavior matches current line-delimited heuristic; otherwise use strict framing with explicit  record separators when available
Automated fuzz tests (5000 randomized chunk splits + escaping cases) pass with 99.99% parse success and zero duplicate invocations in test harness
steps_to_reproduce: Start a streaming chat request that triggers a tool call (structured JSON payload). Interrupt network mid-string (inside quoted value) and reconnect to resume with previous byte index
Send model output that contains nested JSON in a single field (e.g., a string value containing braces and quotes) and confirm the client parser does not prematurely close the object
Configure low max_tokens to force truncation while still emitting partial JSON and observe if downstream tool receives a partial call
Run agent harness with malformed escape sequences (\" and bad unicode) and verify server-side sanitizer either rejects or repairs deterministically
design_decisions: Adopt explicit framing token (0x02) as preferred production path for new SDKs; fall back to bracket balance + escape-aware scan when framing absent
Use a streaming state machine that tracks bracket depth, string-mode, and escape state rather than simple newline heuristics
Introduce optional resume_token: base64(<connection-id>|<last-byte-offset>|<checksum>) included in stream events for reliable resume
Idempotency: prefer a caller-provided call_id; if missing, compute deterministic SHA256 over sorted keys and stable leading text (model prefix) to avoid duplicates
Compatibility mode toggled via request parameter so legacy clients continue unchanged during rollout
implementation_notes: Server: extend streaming runtime parser module (runtime/streaming/parser.go) with state-machine and resume-token generation
Client SDKs (python/js/go): add safe_stream.json_reconstructor and opt-in framing support; expose resume_token in stream events
Router: ensure partial-capture logs contain last-good-offset and checksum for each connection to diagnose truncation incidents
Observability: add metrics stream_parse_failures, stream_duplicate_calls, resume_success_rate; dashboard on Console under 'Streaming > Structured JSON'
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed. PoC state-machine parser implemented in python harness to validate bracket/escape approach (PR link in related_prs). Found multiple failure modes when nested JSON appears inside string values.
2026-03-04: Design review with PM and DX. Agreed on resume_token format and fallback bracket heuristic. Decided not to block on universal framing rollout; opt-in in SDKs.

2026-03-07: Server-side patch started. Parser module unit tests added (edgecases for unicode and backslash-heavy strings). First integration run against dedicated runtime shows reduced parse_failures from 0.6% to 0.04% on synthetic corpus.
2026-03-10: Client SDK changes drafted for JS and Python. Need QA sign-off on compatibility mode. Added fuzz suite to CI (5000 randomized chunkings).
blockers: Need consensus on idempotency semantics when model output lacks stable keys — affects external connectors (Zapier, internal actions)
Resume token encryption: KMS integration required for production resume tokens to avoid leaking connection identifiers
SDK release coordination: rolling framing change requires cross-team release plan (web SDK, mobile, internal agent)
test_plan: Unit tests covering: escape sequences, unicode escapes, multi-chunk string boundaries, unbalanced brackets recovery
Integration tests running against hosted and dedicated runtimes including simulated network flaps and reconnects
Fuzz tests: random chunk boundaries across 5000 corpus messages including nested JSON-in-string cases
End-to-end agent harness verifying zero duplicate tool invocations under simulated retries
Canary rollout on dedicated clusters with metrics gating (stream_parse_failures < 0.1% and duplicate_calls == 0 for 48h)
rollback_plan: If duplicate tool calls or parse regressions detected during canary, immediately toggle compatibility mode on router by config flag, revert streaming parser to previous implementation, and roll new parser as a soft-launch behind explicit query parameter; notify affected customers.
notes: Avoid naive 'count braces' approach — must respect string-mode and escaped quotes
Truncation handling should prefer safe-no-op rather than best-effort partial call; prefer postponing side-effect until finalization when possible
Communicate change to Integrations team; provide migration guide for call_id and resume_token
Consider adding a small ack event from server after tool-call accepted by downstream connector to allow client confirmation
